Unsupervised filter that scores each feature without a target

Source: R/fs_unsupervised.R
fs_unsupervised.Rd

Scores each column of data with a summary that ignores any outcome (variance, spread, missingness, or number of distinct values) and keeps or drops each column by comparing its score with threshold.

Usage

fs_unsupervised(
  data,
  method = c("variance", "mad", "iqr", "range", "missing_prop", "n_unique"),
  threshold = 0,
  direction = c("above", "below"),
  action = c("keep", "remove"),
  include_equal = FALSE,
  na_rm = TRUE,
  output = c("result", "matrix", "dt", "data.frame", "mask", "indices", "names", "list"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame, data.table, or matrix whose columns are all numeric. Every column is a candidate feature. The input is copied, never modified in place.

method

One of "variance" (default), "mad", "iqr", "range", "missing_prop", or "n_unique". See Details.

threshold

Non-negative, finite number compared with each feature's score. Default 0. Each method has its own scale (a variance is in squared units, "missing_prop" lies in [0, 1], "n_unique" is a count), so a threshold chosen for one method does not carry over to another.

direction

"above" (default) or "below": which side of threshold a score must fall on to meet the condition.

action

"keep" (default) retains the features that meet the condition; "remove" drops them.

include_equal

Logical. If TRUE, a score equal to threshold meets the condition. Default FALSE.

na_rm

Logical. If TRUE (the default), NAs are removed before computing "variance", "mad", "iqr", and "range"; if FALSE, an NA in a column makes its score NA under those methods. "missing_prop" and "n_unique" ignore na_rm.

output

Shape of the return value.

  • "result" (default): an fs_result object (see Value).

  • "matrix", "dt", "data.frame": the selected features as a numeric matrix, a data.table, or a data.frame.

  • "mask": logical vector of length ncol(data), named after the columns of data; TRUE marks a selected column.

  • "indices": integer positions of the selected columns, named after them.

  • "names": character vector of the selected column names.

  • "list": a list with filtered (matrix), mask, indices, names, scores, and meta. meta records method, threshold, direction, action, include_equal, na_rm, n_input_cols, and n_kept_cols.

verbose

Logical; print progress messages. Default FALSE.

Value

With output = "result" (the default), an fs_result object:

  • selected: character vector of selected feature names.

  • scores: named numeric vector with one score per column, in column order, NA where the score is undefined.

  • method: "unsupervised_" followed by the method, for example "unsupervised_variance".

  • task: NA_character_, since there is no target.

  • model: NULL.

  • details: a list holding, in this order, mask (the logical keep-mask over the columns), indices (selected positions, named), filtered (the selected columns as a data.table), threshold, direction, action, and n_features (ncol(data)).

  • call: the matched call.

Any other output returns the shape described under output.

When no feature meets the criteria, a warning is issued and the tabular shapes come back empty. "matrix" and "data.frame" then have zero columns and keep the input row count. The "dt" shape and details$filtered have zero columns and also zero rows, because data.table represents a zero-column table that way.

Details

Use it for the first cleaning pass: dropping constant or near-constant columns, columns that are mostly missing, or columns with too few distinct values. No outcome informs the scores, so it is safe to run before a train/test split. For the same reason it says nothing about whether a feature is useful. A high-variance column can be pure noise and a low-variance one can be your best predictor; fs_supervised() or a model-based method answers that question.

The six values of method:

  • "variance" (default): sample variance (denominator n - 1), in squared units. For values below about 1e-162 in magnitude the variance underflows to 0, so to find constant columns in extreme units use "range" with threshold 0 or "n_unique" with threshold 1.

  • "mad": median absolute deviation from stats::mad(), which multiplies by the consistency constant 1.4826. Scores are on the scale of a standard-deviation estimate, not the raw median absolute deviation; choose thresholds on that scale.

  • "iqr": interquartile range.

  • "range": maximum minus minimum.

  • "missing_prop": proportion of missing values, in [0, 1]. With the default threshold = 0, direction = "above", and action = "keep", this keeps the columns that have any missing values and drops the complete ones, which is almost never what you want. A warning then suggests action = "remove" or direction = "below". The warning fires only when all three of threshold, direction, and action are left at their defaults; passing any one of them explicitly silences it.

  • "n_unique": number of distinct non-NA values.

A feature whose score is NA is never selected, whether action is "keep" or "remove", and a warning reports how many features were excluded this way.

Columns are subset by position, never by name, so duplicated column names cannot pull in the wrong column. Every column needs a non-empty, non-NA name. A matrix keeps its own column names; V1, V2, ... are used only when it has none.

See also

The Filter methods guide, which runs this function on a worked example.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  spread = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 100),
  flat   = c(2, 2, 2, 2, 2),
  gappy  = c(1, NA, 3, NA, 5)
)

# Default: an fs_result
res <- fs_unsupervised(df, method = "variance", threshold = 0.5)
res$selected
#> [1] "spread" "gappy" 
res$scores
#> spread   flat  gappy 
#> 1902.5    0.0    4.0 
res$details$filtered
#>    spread gappy
#>     <num> <num>
#> 1:      1     1
#> 2:      2    NA
#> 3:      3     3
#> 4:      4    NA
#> 5:    100     5

# The classic shapes are still available
fs_unsupervised(df, method = "variance", threshold = 0.5,
                output = "matrix")
#>      spread gappy
#> [1,]      1     1
#> [2,]      2    NA
#> [3,]      3     3
#> [4,]      4    NA
#> [5,]    100     5

# Remove features with missing proportion >= 0.2
fs_unsupervised(df, method = "missing_prop", threshold = 0.2,
                direction = "above", action = "remove",
                include_equal = TRUE, output = "names")
#> [1] "spread" "flat"
